::: {.why}
Every result you have reported so far assumed you traded at a printed close, and the fill model is the component that decides how large a lie that is.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Implement a fill model with a stated price convention and a participation constraint, and say what each assumes.
- Report the difference in your strategy's Sharpe between three fill conventions.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Write qlib/backtest/fills.py with three models behind one interface: fill at the close, fill at the close plus half the spread in the direction you traded, and fill at a volume-weighted price with a participation cap that rejects the excess. The third one produces partial fills, which the portfolio has to handle.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Run the trend follower and the pairs strategy under all three and report the Sharpe under each. Then find the participation rate at which the pairs strategy's fills start being rejected, and note what that says about its capacity before you have any impact model at all.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The engine has a pluggable fill model with three conventions and partial fills, so the price a backtest assumes is a stated configuration rather than a hidden default.
:::
